page: Amazon Web Services c5a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the c5a.xlarge delivers modest performance relative to other instances in its class. In stress-ng CPU tests, both single-core and multi-core performance fall into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak performance in the bottom 25% for both cached and uncached reads and writes, with uncached read bandwidth at 35.51 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core scores are average, but multi-core scores and specialized tasks like software compiling, ray tracing, and image processing fall into the bottom 25%. Cryptographic operations, such as the PassMark CPU encryption test, and single-threaded gzip compression perform at an average level.

The primary tradeoff of the c5a.xlarge is its limited memory capacity and weak multi-threaded scaling, as demonstrated by its poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and weak Redis SET operations. However, the instance offers a cost-effective entry point for dedicated compute resources without the overhead of local storage. It is suitable for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation with moderate memory requirements, such as basic web serving, single-threaded data processing, lightweight cryptography, and small-scale LLM text generation.
